summary: This manuscript provides a rigorous electrodynamic audit of the 71-THz mitochondrial cristae polariton hypothesis, addressing the central subwavelength confinement obstruction. Using a dual-layer verification architecture combining 18 constructive Lean 4 theorems (0 sorry, 0 custom axioms) and 16 canonical exact-Q certificates, the author proves five major results: (i) an exact LST oscillator-strength deficit requiring >16.7x to >100x enhancement; (ii) a fundamental Fabry-Pérot half-wave thickness cutoff (>1188 nm) forbidding single-crista transverse modes; (iii) exact uniaxial EMT and AM-GM damped Lorentz minimum proofs showing fluid bilayers cannot generate negative permittivity at 71 THz; (iv) exact unimodal SL(2, Q) transfer-matrix audits confirming crista stacks sit in the acoustic passband without acting as Bragg mirrors; and (v) aqueous dielectric-loss Q-factor ceilings and H2O/D2O isotopic dual-branch diagnostics.
